solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Got longer articles to spread popular beliefs (9)

indicators.note: the letters are spread out and laid down again in a new order

blocks.note: in = popular, fashionable
the first of the articles, a, the indefinite article
creeds = beliefs; mixed with A to make CREASED

annotation.surface: Newspaper pieces grew longer so as to spread fashionable ideas.
annotation.walkthrough: "Articles" reads as newspaper pieces that grew longer; it only supplies the indefinite article, and "to spread" scrambles it with the beliefs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: a queue that increased grew in length, stretching further down the street.

entries.clue: National Anthem’s introduction bores two hosting King and Queen (5)

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter
to bore is to drill into, so this letter goes inside
a host holds guests inside

blocks.note: two = II in Roman numerals; the first I
R = Rex, king
the first letter of ANTHEM, boring in between R and Q
Q = queen, as on playing cards
the second I of II, closing round R, A and Q

annotation.surface: The opening bars of the national anthem bore two people who are entertaining the royal couple.
annotation.walkthrough: "National Anthem" looks like one phrase, but "National" is the definition on its own and the anthem only lends its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: "National" as a noun means a citizen of some country, and a citizen of Baghdad's country is one example.

entries.clue: Head of unit’s integrated circuit included in authoritative proposal (10,7)

indicators.note: one piece is put inside another

blocks.note: commanding = authoritative; offer = proposal
IC is the standard abbreviation for an integrated circuit, placed inside OFFER

annotation.surface: A unit head's chip is part of a forceful bid.
annotation.walkthrough: The electronics vocabulary makes "unit" look like a component, but it is a military unit.
annotation.definitionFit: In the army, the person in charge of a battalion or regiment holds this title, so it names whoever leads that unit.

entries.clue: He helps move each man around country (6,5)

indicators.note: one piece is placed round another

blocks.note: ea. is the abbreviation for each; it goes around STATE
a state is a country
gent = man

annotation.surface: A helpful removal man working his way round the country.
annotation.walkthrough: "Move" reads as shifting furniture, but it means moving house; an estate agent is what Americans call a realtor.
annotation.definitionFit: An estate agent helps people move house by selling their home.

entries.clue: Royal Engineer’s draining job? (6)

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers are the British Army's engineering corps, and their privates have their own name
to sap strength is to drain it, so one who does that job

annotation.surface: A soldier-engineer whose task is to drain water away.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses come from sap: the military one from digging saps (trenches), the other from sapping energy. The question mark flags the invented sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Sapper is the rank and nickname of a soldier in the Royal Engineers.

entries.clue: Suspect unlikely to take part (8)

blocks.note: suspect as an adjective: open to question, dubious
the sports-page word for an injured player who may miss the match

annotation.surface: A person under suspicion who probably won't join in.
annotation.walkthrough: "Suspect" wants to be a noun, a person, but it is the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Doubtful means questionable, and in sports reporting a player unlikely to play is doubtful.

entries.clue: Sound — that of ceremony? (5)

indicators.note: the word also tells you to go by sound

blocks.note: a rite is a ceremonial act

annotation.surface: A question about what sort of noise a ceremony makes.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sound" does two jobs: it is the definition (sound = correct) and the signal to listen for RITE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sound judgement is correct, accurate and well founded.

entries.clue: Unrealistically positive representation of decorous role (4-8)

indicators.note: the letters are presented in a new form

blocks.note: all twelve letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A flattering portrayal of a well-behaved character.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like theatre criticism, which hides that "decorous role" is simply the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To see through rose-coloured glasses is to be unrealistically optimistic.

entries.clue: I’m astonished about papers supporting rat’s abandoned wife (5,5)

indicators.note: one piece goes around another
in a down clue, a support sits underneath

blocks.note: a grass is British slang for an informer, a rat
wow! expresses astonishment; it goes about ID
ID = identity papers

annotation.surface: Someone amazed at the documents showing an informer has deserted his wife.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rat" reads as a deserting husband; it is the informer, and in a down clue the papers support it by sitting underneath.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a wife whose husband is away for long periods, left on her own.

entries.clue: Article ending in Saint Paul’s Second Letter to The Corinthians (5)

indicators.note: take the last letter of the next word
take the second letter of the word

blocks.note: the is the definite article
the last letter of SAINT
the second letter of PAUL

annotation.surface: A reference to St Paul's second epistle to the Corinthians.
annotation.walkthrough: The Bible reference is a disguise: the Corinthians were Greek, so a letter to them is a Greek letter. "Letter" works in both the wordplay and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, the one the Corinthians used.

entries.clue: Corrupts spy brought back to safeguard lives (7)

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so the word reads right to left
the outer word protects what goes inside it

blocks.note: to snoop is to spy; SNOOP reads backwards as POONS
is = lives, exists; placed inside PO…ONS

annotation.surface: A traitor sent home to protect people's lives is corrupting them.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lives" looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb: exists, IS.
annotation.definitionFit: To poison someone's mind is to corrupt it.

entries.clue: Riddle about source of Italian pizza topping (9)

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to pepper with shot is to riddle with holes
on = about, concerning
the first letter of ITALIAN

annotation.surface: A puzzle about where an Italian pizza topping comes from.
annotation.walkthrough: "Riddle" poses as a puzzle, but it is the verb: to fill with holes.
annotation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy sausage sliced onto pizzas.

entries.clue: Individual questioning position adopted by dodgy rentier (11)

indicators.note: one piece is taken in by another
the letters are unreliable, so rearrange them

blocks.note: RENTIER rearranged, wrapped around VIEW
a position on a question is a view

annotation.surface: A single person being quizzed about a stance taken by a shady landlord.
annotation.walkthrough: "Individual questioning" reads as a person under interrogation, but it is the one doing the asking. A rentier lives on rents and investments.
annotation.definitionFit: Read "questioning" as an active participle: the person doing the asking in a job interview or on a chat show.

entries.clue: Animal with a varied diet consisting mainly of fruit (5)

indicators.note: most of the word, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: ORANGE, a fruit, without its last letter

annotation.surface: An omnivore that nonetheless eats mostly fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: The dietary detail is true of orangutans, which are largely fruit-eaters, so the surface works as a description too.
annotation.definitionFit: Orang is short for orangutan, the great ape.

entries.clue: Who might investigate elaborate hustle? (6)

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: HUSTLE rearranged

annotation.surface: Asking who would look into an intricate con.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a detective is exactly who would investigate an elaborate scam.
annotation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, someone who investigates.

entries.clue: Acknowledge passage of mine contains start of message (5)

indicators.note: the tunnel contains, holds inside it, the letter that follows
the first letter of the word

blocks.note: an adit is a horizontal passage into a mine
the first letter of MESSAGE, inside AD…IT

annotation.surface: Owning up that a tunnel of mine holds the beginning of a note.
annotation.walkthrough: "Of mine" reads as belonging to me, but it is a mine shaft. ADIT is a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: owning up to a fault or conceding a point are both ways of accepting the truth.

entries.clue: Former state comprising capital of Poland and part of Soviet Union (7)

indicators.note: the capital letter, the first one

blocks.note: the first letter of POLAND
Russia was the largest republic of the USSR

annotation.surface: A historical state made up of Warsaw and a Soviet republic.
annotation.walkthrough: "Capital of Poland" pushes Warsaw; it is only the capital letter. The geography fits too: Prussia straddled modern Poland and Russia.
annotation.definitionFit: Prussia was a German kingdom and state, abolished in 1947.

entries.clue: Being in exile forfeits right to go into details (9)

indicators.note: the word gives up the letter named

blocks.note: an expatriate lives outside their own country
R = right; removed from EXPATRIATE

annotation.surface: Living abroad costs someone the right to elaborate.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a loss of civil rights; the right lost is just the letter R.
annotation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length, going into detail.

entries.clue: Most of teaching unit is rehashed for mock (11)

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter, so one is dropped
the letters are hashed up again into a new order

blocks.note: TEACHING without its last letter
joins the anagram as it is

annotation.surface: A teaching module reworked to serve as a practice exam.
annotation.walkthrough: "Teaching unit" looks like a single item with "most of" applying to both words, but only TEACHING is cut. "Mock" is the adjective, fake, not a practice exam.
annotation.definitionFit: Mock as an adjective means imitation, as in mock Tudor houses, which are not genuine.

entries.clue: Onset of fear when entering dramatic location? (5,6)

definitions.text: Onset of fear when entering dramatic location?

indicators.note: the first letter of the word
the letter goes into the other piece

blocks.note: stage right is a position on a theatre stage
the first letter of FEAR, entering STAGE RIGHT

annotation.surface: The nerves that hit an actor stepping onto the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: stage fright is fear that strikes as you walk on stage.
annotation.definitionFit: Stage fright is the nervousness performers feel before or during an appearance.

entries.clue: Pull again and screw around (6)

indicators.note: to turn something around is to face it the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a screw is British prison slang for a warder, a prison guard; read it backwards

annotation.surface: Someone pulling again and fooling about.
annotation.walkthrough: "Screw around" reads as a phrasal verb, but "screw" is a noun, the prison officer.
annotation.definitionFit: To redraw a card or a pint is to draw, pull, it again.

entries.clue: Dazzling display on a revolutionary English company’s range of work (10)

indicators.note: a revolution turns the word round

blocks.note: re = on, concerning
per = a, as in forty miles per (a) gallon
a riot of colour is a dazzling display; RIOT turned round
E = English

annotation.surface: A spectacular show put on by a radical English theatre troupe.
annotation.walkthrough: "Revolutionary English company" reads as one radical group, but "company’s" belongs to the definition and "revolutionary" turns RIOT round.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre company's repertoire is the range of works it can perform.

entries.clue: Constructive activity gradually getting more intense (8)

blocks.note: the trade of putting up houses and offices
as tension or a storm mounts, growing stronger step by step

annotation.surface: Useful work that steadily ramps up.
annotation.walkthrough: "Constructive" reads as helpful, but it means literally to do with construction.
annotation.definitionFit: Building is both construction work and a gradual increase, as in a building storm.

entries.clue: Understand board is ready for acquisition (8)

blocks.note: to get a joke is to understand it
a table is a board, as in a festive board

annotation.surface: Someone realises the company's directors are open to a takeover.
annotation.walkthrough: "Board" and "acquisition" set up a boardroom takeover; the board is just a table.
annotation.definitionFit: Something gettable is obtainable, there to be acquired.

entries.clue: Stupefying work I put away (6)

blocks.note: op. = opus, a work
I as it stands
to put away food is to eat it

annotation.surface: Someone boasting of the mind-numbing work they have filed away.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stupefying" looks like amazing, but it is the literal sense: dulling the senses. OPIATE here is the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: An opiate drug is stupefying, inducing sleep and dulling the senses.

entries.clue: Connected with cast’s broadcast completely (7,3,7)

indicators.note: on air you hear the word, not its spelling

blocks.note: on the phone, once connected you are through
and = with
cast = threw

annotation.surface: A comment on how the actors are linked to a broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cast" pushes a group of actors next to "broadcast", but it is the past tense of throw.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone British through and through is British in every fibre, wholly so.

entries.clue: Toxic atmosphere found among academia’s managers (6)

indicators.note: the answer sits among the letters of the next words

blocks.note: acadeMIA’S MAnagers

annotation.surface: A poisonous culture among university administrators.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a jibe at university managers, and the metaphor is apt: a miasma is also a pervasive bad atmosphere.
annotation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious vapour, or figuratively an oppressive atmosphere.

entries.clue: Reversed trend, heading off praise for position taken by journalist? (10)

indicators.note: a reversed car goes backwards, and so do these letters
the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: tide = trend, as in the tide of opinion; turned round
WORSHIP, praise, without its first letter

annotation.surface: A columnist changing tack and dropping the flattery.
annotation.walkthrough: "Reversed trend" reads as a market turning, but it is TIDE turned round. The question mark flags a definition by example: the journalist is an editor.
annotation.definitionFit: An editorship is the post held by the editor of a publication.

entries.clue: Named suspect in photo creating widespread disorder (8)

indicators.note: the letters are not to be trusted, so rearrange them
one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: pic = photo; it wraps around ANDEM
NAMED rearranged

annotation.surface: A named suspect caught on camera sparks riots.
annotation.walkthrough: "Disorder" suggests rioting; here it is a disease, spread worldwide.
annotation.definitionFit: A pandemic is a disease, a disorder, spread across a whole country or the world.

entries.clue: Divine alien? (3,2,4,5)

blocks.note: divine in the gushing sense: heavenly, marvellous, sublime
an alien is literally from outside this world

annotation.surface: Asking whether a god is really an extraterrestrial.
annotation.walkthrough: "Divine" sounds heavenly but means simply marvellous; the question mark flags the literal reading of "alien".
annotation.definitionFit: Out of this world means superb, and literally extraterrestrial.

entries.clue: Clears head raising matter concerning supervisor finishing early (6,2)

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising turns the letters to read upwards
the word stops before its last letter

blocks.note: pus is the matter in a wound
re = concerning
BOSS without its last letter

annotation.surface: A headache clearing as a boil under the boss's supervision comes to a head.
annotation.walkthrough: PUS, RE and BOS are laid down in clue order, then the whole string is read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who sobers up clears their head after drinking.

entries.clue: Support for individuals with bills to settle (5)

blocks.note: individuals with bills are birds, and their support is a perch
the verb for birds settling down for the night

annotation.surface: A debt charity helping people pay what they owe.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bills" are beaks, not debts, and "to settle" is the second definition rather than paying up.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses come from birds: the perch they sleep on, and the act of settling there for the night.

entries.clue: Demonstrator in disreputable group (6)

blocks.note: one who shows or demonstrates something; this sense rhymes with mower
British slang for a useless or contemptible lot, the same word as a burst of rain

annotation.surface: A protester mixed up with a bad crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: "Demonstrator" suggests a protester; it means someone who demonstrates, shows. The two senses are pronounced differently.
annotation.definitionFit: A shower is someone who shows, and in British slang a shambolic bunch.

entries.clue: Itchy feet could be symptomatic of this condition (10)

definitions.text: Itchy feet could be symptomatic of this condition

blocks.note: the surface reading: a skin complaint such as athlete's foot
the meant reading: itchy feet is the idiom for a restless urge to travel

annotation.surface: A doctor's note on what an itching foot might indicate.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical words "symptomatic" and "condition" push a skin disease; "itchy feet" is the everyday idiom for wanting to travel.
annotation.definitionFit: Wanderlust is a strong desire to travel, which people describe as having itchy feet.

entries.clue: Discourage drinking by right (6)

indicators.note: the outer word takes in the other, as a drinker takes in drink

blocks.note: to deter is to discourage
x = by, as in 3 x 4 (three by four); placed inside DE…TER

annotation.surface: Advice to put people off drinking, by rights.
annotation.walkthrough: "By right" reads as a phrase, but "by" is the multiplication sign and "right" is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Dexter is the heraldic and Latin word for right-hand.

entries.clue: Meeting lays to rest notice following reorganisation (12)

indicators.note: the letters come after a reorganisation into a new order

blocks.note: to inter is to bury, lay to rest
NOTICE rearranged

annotation.surface: A committee that shelves an announcement after a restructure.
annotation.walkthrough: "Meeting" suggests a committee, but it is where two lines meet.
annotation.definitionFit: An intersection is a meeting point of roads or lines.

entries.clue: Initially investigated if de facto changes performed authorized role (10)

indicators.note: what comes initially is at the start, so only the opening letter
the letters change their order

blocks.note: the first letter of INVESTIGATED
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: An inquiry into whether informal changes meant someone was acting in an official capacity.
annotation.walkthrough: "De facto" sounds like legal Latin to be translated; its letters are simply fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: To officiate is to perform an official duty, such as a referee or a priest does.

entries.clue: Chamber piece inspired by observation (11)

indicators.note: breathed in, so taken inside the other word

blocks.note: a comment is an observation
part = piece; placed inside COM…MENT

annotation.surface: A piece of chamber music composed after something the composer noticed.
annotation.walkthrough: "Chamber piece" suggests chamber music, but "Chamber" is the definition alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a separate enclosed section, such as one in a railway carriage or a ship's hull.

entries.clue: Surge of immigrants possibly belonging to unstable state (6)

blocks.note: in = belonging to, as in a member in a club
flux is a state of continual change

annotation.surface: A wave of migration from a country in turmoil.
annotation.walkthrough: "Possibly" marks immigrants as just one example of an influx.
annotation.definitionFit: An influx is an arrival of large numbers, such as of immigrants.

entries.clue: Shudder at minor injuries inflicted during attack by men (5)

blocks.note: ABH is actual bodily harm, a less serious assault charge in English law
OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

annotation.surface: Recoiling at the cuts and bruises from an assault by a gang.
annotation.walkthrough: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a British criminal charge for an assault causing injury short of grievous harm.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to loathe something so deeply it makes you recoil in disgust.

entries.clue: Software industry (11)

blocks.note: a program you run, shortened to app
industry in the sense of diligence, steady hard work

annotation.surface: The software business.
annotation.walkthrough: "Software industry" reads as one phrase; "industry" is diligence, not a business sector.
annotation.definitionFit: Application means both a computer program and steady effort.

entries.clue: Might scheme finish off bankrupt energy supplier? (5,5)

indicators.note: take the last letter of the word

blocks.note: might = power
a scheme is a plan
the last letter of BANKRUPT

annotation.surface: Wondering if a plot might ruin an insolvent energy firm.
annotation.walkthrough: "Might" reads as the verb in a question, but it is the noun, strength.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a power station, the installation that generates electricity for the grid.

entries.clue: Put in new order for remix of Memories on disc (14)

indicators.note: the letters are mixed again into a new track

blocks.note: all fourteen letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A record label ordering a new mix of an album of memories.
annotation.walkthrough: "Order" reads as sequence, but it means a commission, as a new order for work.
annotation.definitionFit: To recommission something is to order it again.

entries.clue: Put off key deficiency in Asian country’s attitude (9)

indicators.note: the word is lacking the letter named

blocks.note: INDIA'S; minus the key A it becomes INDIS

a pose is an attitude, a stance

annotation.surface: A country's stance puts a would-be visitor off.
annotation.walkthrough: "Key deficiency" sounds like a crucial weakness; key is the musical note A, which INDIA'S loses.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal verb meaning to make someone disinclined or unwilling, the root of being indisposed to help.

entries.clue: Essential blow phased out computing device (3,5)

blocks.note: key = essential
a punch is a blow

annotation.surface: A crucial knockout that retired a machine.
annotation.walkthrough: "Phased out" belongs to the definition: a key punch is an obsolete machine for punching data cards.

entries.clue: Agree method of eliminating change? (8)

blocks.note: loose change is coins
-cide means killing, as in pesticide

annotation.surface: A question about how to get rid of loose change.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is to read COINCIDE as coin-icide, the killing of coins; the question mark owns up to the made-up word.
annotation.definitionFit: Accounts that coincide agree with each other.

entries.clue: Make a mistake with message (6)

blocks.note: to err is to make a mistake
and = with

annotation.surface: Getting a text wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: "Message" is the old sense of an errand: a trip to deliver something, still used in Scotland as "going for the messages".
annotation.definitionFit: An errand, like a message, is a short trip to deliver or collect something.

entries.clue: Folk on social media in what way entertaining spectacle with restricted view (8)

blocks.note: peeps is online slang for people
how = in what way

annotation.surface: Social media users asking how some limited-view show entertains.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is long and descriptive: a peepshow is viewed through a small hole.
annotation.definitionFit: A peepshow is an entertainment viewed through a small aperture.

entries.clue: First class spinner follows helpful advice (6)

indicators.note: this piece comes after the other

blocks.note: a tip is a helpful piece of advice
a top is a spinning toy; it follows TIP

annotation.surface: A top-grade spin bowler taking good advice.
annotation.walkthrough: "Spinner" suggests a cricket spin bowler; it is the child's spinning top.
annotation.definitionFit: Dated informal praise for something excellent, in the very best condition.

entries.clue: Old on-line journal includes name of slender figure? (6)

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: O = old
a blog is an online journal; it goes round N
N = name

annotation.surface: An old online diary naming a thin person.
annotation.walkthrough: "Slender figure" suggests a slim person; here it is a geometric figure, longer than it is wide.
annotation.definitionFit: An oblong is a rectangle longer than it is wide, a slender shape.

entries.clue: Free to think again seemingly (6)

indicators.note: the answer only appears to break into these parts

blocks.note: re- = again
to deem is to think

annotation.surface: Freedom to reconsider, apparently.
annotation.walkthrough: "Seemingly" admits that RE-DEEM is not the word's real origin, just what it looks like.
annotation.definitionFit: To redeem a captive is to free them by paying a ransom.

entries.clue: Peach skin’s flipping lovely nap? (6,5)

entries.clue: Revise warning as a result of temperature rising (5)

entries.clue: Employ specialist denied position originally (5)

the first letter of the word

the first letter of POSITION; removed from EXPERT

entries.clue: Support for light punishment of cruel bad man (11)

indicators.note: the letters are knocked about

blocks.note: all eleven letters rearranged

annotation.surface: Backing for a lenient sentence for a cruel villain.

annotation.definitionFit: A candelabrum is a branched holder for candles, a support for light.

entries.clue: Second unsatisfactory service upset driver using this establishment (5)

entries.clue: For Americans, exactly where one might find visual aids? (2,3,4)

entries.clue: Idiotic ideas in inefficient stores (7)

indicators.note: the words store the answer inside them

blocks.note: ideAS IN INEfficient

annotation.surface: Foolish schemes in badly run shops.

entries.clue: Northerners instinctively know to give up first time (5)

entries.clue: Taking out line of rubbish clogging up entrance (7)

entries.clue: Great man’s relations inhibited by effect of The Sun’s coverage (5)

blocks.note: a tan is what sunshine on the skin produces
